P.No.1 of 24 Bk Date of accident : 26.09.2017 Result of accident : Grievous injury(Amputation) Date of filing of Petition : 19.01.2018 Date of Decision : 05.08.2025 Award 1.
texts.facts: The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Harendra Bhati suffered grievous injury and amputation of left lower limb. An application u/s 166(1) MV Act was accordingly filed by the claimant/petitioner. Brief facts of the case are that on 26.09.2017 at about 04:30 p.m., petitioner/injured Harendra Bhati was travelling on his Scooty number UP-16-BL-0253 from Delhi to his residence at Dadri. When petitioner reached near Halka OP Kasba Bypass Dadri, Gautam Budh Nagar, a Honda Amaze car bearing no.UP-81-BN-1563 came from behind, driven rashly and negligently and hit the Scooty of petitioner. Petitioner sustained serious injuries in this accident and was rushed to Yashoda Super Specialty hospital. Petitioner underwent surgeries in which his left lower limb below the knee was amputated. 3. An FIR no.0749/2017, dated 07.10.2017 was registered u/s 279/338/427 of IPC at PS Dadri, U.P. Matter was investigated and a chargesheet was filed before concerned criminal court while claim petition was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Respondent no.1 is the driver, respondent no.2 is the owner and respondent no.3/Oriental Insurance company is the insurance company with which the offending vehicle was insured. 5. Despite service of notice, Respondent no.1 and 2 did not appear and were proceeded ex-parte vide order datedCHARU 06.08.2019. Digitally signed by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA In its reply, respondent no.3 has refuted the occurrence of accident and suspected collusion between the petitioner and respondent alleging an unexplained delay of 11 days in lodging FIR. It is, however, admitted that on the date of accident offending vehicle was insured. 6. Vide order dated 06.08.2019, following issues were framed. 1. Whether the petitioner suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 26.09.2017 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. UP-81BN-1563 being driven by R1, owned by R2 and insured with R3? OPP 2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom? OPP. 3. Relief. 7. To prove his claim, petitioner Harendra Bhati led his evidence by examining himself as PW-1. He tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He testified on the lines of the claim petition and deposed that on 26.09.2017 at about 4.30 p.m. he was travelling by Scooty No.UP-16-BL-0253 from Delhi to his residence Dadri. When he reached near Halka OP Kasba Bypass Dadri , Honda Amaze car bearing no.UP-81- BN-1563 came from behind driven in rash and negligent away and hit him. He sustained serious injuries and was removed to Yashoda Super Specialty hospital, NOIDA for treatment. He sustained injuries over left upper limb and lower limb. He underwent four surgeries. After accident, he was removed to Mohan Swarup hospital. He got admitted to Yashoda Harendra Bhati vs Ajay on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15477647/ 2 hospital on 30.09.2017 and discharged on 07.10.2017, he was again admitted CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.08.05 17:27:44 +0530 MACT No.226/18 Harendra Bhati v. Ajay. P.No.3 of 24 BK on 18.11.2017 and discharged on 20.11.2017 and again admitted on 20.11.2017 and discharged on 08.12.2017. During the treatment he was operated on 19.11.2017 where his mid foot of left leg was amputated. He was discharged on 20.11.2017. PW-1 further deposed that he was 31 years old at the time of accident, doing job of milk supply and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m. He deposed that after the accident, he became permanently disabled. He spent Rs.15 lac on medical treatment and requires Rs.7 lac for artificial limb. He relied upon certified copy of chargesheet as Ex.PW-1/1, photocopy of Aadhar card as Ex.PW-1/2, Discharge summary as Ex.PW-1/3, Treatment bills as Ex.PW-1/4, physical disability certificate as Ex.PW-1/5 and photocopy of DL of petitioner as Ex.PW-1/6. He was duly cross-examined by Ld. counsel for insurance company/respondent no.3. No evidence was led on behalf of the respondents. 8. Final arguments in details were addressed on behalf of the claimant/injured and the insurance company. the petitioner suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 26.09.2017 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. UP-81BN-1563 being driven by R1, owned by R2 and insured with R3? OPP 9. Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.
texts.arguments: Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & Ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. The petitioner admitted that the accident occurred at a time when he was joining the main road through service road. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 12. Further, driver of the offending vehicle has not challenged or denied by evidence, his rashness or negligence in driving of the offending vehicle or committing the accident. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. 15. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680. The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. 16.6. Observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajkumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. is quoted hereunder: 19. Further, in view of decision of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Chander Jeet Singh vs. Mahavir Singh MAC.APP110/2006, this sum awarded to the petitioner is directed to be kept in fixed deposit of initially for a period of 2 years. 28.
